answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim a reward, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit proves fraud. Because one person can mint thousands of keys but must fund each separately, splitting into sybils multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. Honest agents recover their deposits; an attacker pays in locked funds, audit exposure, and lost stake. The rule can wander across task types without changing, whether agents trade shale data or help a project recover from a nadir.
